interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body:
The prognosis is influenced by several factors, including the preoperative PSA of 11.7 and the pathological T-stage of pT3a with extraprostatic extension noted in the surgical report. Positive features include negative surgical margins and no seminal vesicle invasion or lymphovascular invasion documented. A significant limitation is that no lymph nodes were removed, meaning nodal status cannot be assessed, which widens uncertainty regarding risk stratification. The biopsy findings (Gleason 3+3) are consistent with the prostatectomy specimen grade (ISUP group 1).

The trajectory of postoperative PSA and subsequent follow-up data would significantly revise this prognosis. Currently, there is no information available to assess post-operative biochemical recurrence risk beyond the initial pathological findings. The absence of nodal sampling prevents definitive staging regarding regional spread. The fixed estimated horizon is 69.39 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 45.11–93.68 months; its coverage has not been validated.
